title: CEFR expansion pack 01
description: Large vocabulary and communicative-function expansion plus planned grammar roadmap. Draft rules are not active until implementation and contrastive tests pass.

grammarRules.title: Use singular countable nouns with a determiner
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa determinante con sustantivos contables singulares
grammarRules.explanation: A singular countable noun normally needs a determiner in a noun phrase.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Un sustantivo contable singular normalmente necesita un determinante.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form regular plural nouns
grammarRules.explanation: Most countable nouns form the plural with -s or -es.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La mayoría de sustantivos contables forman el plural con -s o -es.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Choose this/that and these/those
grammarRules.explanation: Use this/that for singular nouns and these/those for plural nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa this/that con singular y these/those con plural.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use possessive adjectives
grammarRules.explanation: Possessive adjectives agree with the possessor, not the thing possessed.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los posesivos concuerdan con quien posee, no con el objeto poseído.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form present simple questions with do/does
grammarRules.titleEs: Forma preguntas en presente simple con do/does
grammarRules.explanation: Use do/does before the subject; use the base verb after does.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa do/does antes del sujeto y el verbo base después de does.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use do not/does not + base verb
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa do not/does not + verbo base
grammarRules.explanation: Present simple negatives use do not/does not plus the base verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La negación en presente simple usa do not/does not más verbo base.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Place frequency adverbs in the usual position
grammarRules.explanation: Frequency adverbs usually precede a main verb but follow be.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los adverbios de frecuencia suelen preceder al verbo principal, pero siguen a be.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Build the present continuous
grammarRules.explanation: Use be + verb-ing for actions in progress or temporary situations.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be + verbo-ing para acciones en curso o situaciones temporales.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use was/were in the past
grammarRules.explanation: Use was with I/he/she/it and were with you/we/they.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa was con I/he/she/it y were con you/we/they.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form regular past verbs
grammarRules.titleEs: Forma el pasado de verbos regulares
grammarRules.explanation: Regular verbs commonly take -ed in the past; spelling varies by verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los verbos regulares suelen tomar -ed en pasado; la ortografía depende del verbo.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use did + base verb in past questions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa did + verbo base en preguntas pasadas
grammarRules.explanation: After did, use the base form of the main verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de did, usa la forma base del verbo principal.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use did not + base verb
grammarRules.explanation: Past simple negatives use did not plus the base form.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La negación en pasado simple usa did not más la forma base.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use can + base verb for ability
grammarRules.explanation: A modal is followed by the base form of the verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Un modal va seguido de la forma base del verbo.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use should + base verb for advice
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa should + verbo base para aconsejar
grammarRules.explanation: Should is followed by the base form, without to.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Should va seguido del verbo base, sin to.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form common comparative adjectives
grammarRules.explanation: Short adjectives often take -er; longer adjectives commonly use more.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los adjetivos cortos suelen usar -er; los largos, more.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use superlatives to compare three or more
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa superlativos para comparar tres o más
grammarRules.explanation: Superlatives commonly use the + -est or the most.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los superlativos suelen usar the + -est o the most.
incorrect: It is the most easiest task

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Choose much/many with nouns
grammarRules.explanation: Use many with countable plurals and much with uncountable nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa many con plurales contables y much con incontables.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use some/any in common contexts
grammarRules.explanation: Some is common in affirmative clauses; any is common in questions and negatives, with exceptions.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Some es frecuente en afirmativas; any en preguntas y negativas, con excepciones.
incorrect: We do not have some tools

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Match there is/there are to number
grammarRules.explanation: Use there is with singular or uncountable nouns and there are with plural nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa there is con singular o incontables y there are con plurales.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use in/on/at for common time expressions
grammarRules.explanation: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years and parts of the day.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa at para horas, on para días y fechas e in para meses, años y partes del día.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use common prepositions of place
grammarRules.explanation: In, on, under, next to and between describe different spatial relationships.
grammarRules.explanationEs: In, on, under, next to y between describen relaciones espaciales diferentes.
examples: The sensor is under the table
incorrect: The sensor is between the table

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use be going to for intentions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa be going to para intenciones
grammarRules.explanation: Use be + going to + base verb for plans and intentions.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be + going to + verbo base para planes e intenciones.
examples: We are going to test the robot
incorrect: We going to test the robot

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use will + base verb
grammarRules.explanation: Will is followed by the base form of the verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Will va seguido de la forma base del verbo.
incorrect: I will to explain the project

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Build the present perfect
grammarRules.explanation: Use have/has + past participle for experiences and past actions connected to now.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa have/has + participio para experiencias y acciones pasadas relacionadas con el presente.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Distinguish present perfect and finished past time
grammarRules.titleEs: Distingue presente perfecto y pasado terminado
grammarRules.explanation: Use past simple with a finished past time; present perfect generally avoids specific finished-time markers.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa pasado simple con tiempo pasado terminado; el presente perfecto suele evitar esos marcadores.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form the first conditional
grammarRules.explanation: Use if + present simple and will + base verb for a likely future condition and result.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa if + presente simple y will + verbo base para una condición futura probable.
examples: If it rains, we will stay inside
incorrect: If it will rain, we will stay inside

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use who/which/that in defining clauses
grammarRules.explanation: Use who for people and which for things; that can often refer to either in defining clauses.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa who para personas y which para cosas; that puede referirse a ambos.
examples: The student who built the robot is here
incorrect: The student which built the robot is here

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use to + verb to express purpose
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa to + verbo para expresar propósito
grammarRules.explanation: The to-infinitive commonly explains why someone does something.
grammarRules.explanationEs: El infinitivo con to suele explicar para qué se hace algo.
examples: I use an app to practice English
incorrect: I use an app for practice English

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use too and enough with adjectives
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa too y enough con adjetivos
grammarRules.explanation: Too usually precedes an adjective; enough usually follows it.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Too suele preceder al adjetivo; enough suele ir después.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use although and however appropriately
grammarRules.explanation: Although introduces a subordinate contrast clause; however often links clauses with punctuation.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Although introduce una subordinada concesiva; however suele conectar oraciones con puntuación apropiada.
examples: Although it was hard, we finished
incorrect: Although it was hard, but we finished

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Express cause and result with because/so
grammarRules.titleEs: Expresa causa y resultado con because/so
grammarRules.explanation: Because introduces a reason; so introduces a result.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Because introduce una razón; so introduce un resultado.
examples: It was late, so we left
incorrect: Because it was late, so we left

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use statement word order in indirect questions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa orden afirmativo en preguntas indirectas
grammarRules.explanation: Indirect questions use subject + verb order after Could you tell me.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Las preguntas indirectas usan sujeto + verbo después de Could you tell me.
examples: Could you tell me where the lab is?
incorrect: Could you tell me where is the lab?

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Distinguish general plural nouns from specific nouns
grammarRules.titleEs: Distingue plurales generales de nombres específicos
grammarRules.explanation: Plural countable nouns can appear without the when speaking generally; the signals a specific group.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los plurales contables pueden ir sin the en sentido general; the identifica un grupo específico.
incorrect: The robots can help people (general meaning)

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Distinguish stop doing and stop to do
grammarRules.titleEs: Distingue stop doing y stop to do
grammarRules.explanation: Stop doing means end an activity; stop to do means pause another activity to do something.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Stop doing significa terminar una actividad; stop to do significa detenerse para hacer otra cosa.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Choose common make/do collocations
grammarRules.explanation: English uses conventional collocations such as make a decision and do homework.
grammarRules.explanationEs: El inglés usa colocaciones convencionales como make a decision y do homework.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use depend on
grammarRules.explanation: The verb depend is commonly followed by on.
grammarRules.explanationEs: El verbo depend suele ir seguido de on.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use listen to
grammarRules.explanation: Listen normally takes to before the thing or person heard.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Listen normalmente lleva to antes de aquello que se escucha.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use explain something to someone
grammarRules.explanation: Explain is commonly followed by the thing explained and then to + person.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Explain suele ir seguido de lo que se explica y luego to + persona.
examples: I explained the rule to my students
incorrect: I explained my students the rule

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use object pronouns after verbs and prepositions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa pronombres de objeto después de verbos y preposiciones
grammarRules.explanation: Use me, him, her, us and them as objects, not I/he/she/we/they.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa me, him, her, us y them como objetos, no I/he/she/we/they.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use reflexive pronouns when subject and object are the same
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa reflexivos cuando sujeto y objeto son iguales
grammarRules.explanation: Use myself, yourself and similar forms when the subject acts on itself.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa myself, yourself y formas similares cuando el sujeto actúa sobre sí mismo.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Distinguish -ed and -ing adjectives
grammarRules.explanation: Many -ed adjectives describe feelings; -ing adjectives describe what causes them.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Muchos adjetivos en -ed describen sentimientos; los de -ing describen lo que los provoca.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Avoid a/an with uncountable nouns
grammarRules.explanation: Uncountable nouns such as information and equipment do not normally take a/an.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los incontables como information y equipment normalmente no llevan a/an.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Form basic question tags with matching auxiliaries
grammarRules.explanation: A positive statement usually takes a negative tag; auxiliary and pronoun must match.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Una afirmación positiva suele llevar coletilla negativa; auxiliar y pronombre deben concordar.
examples: You are a teacher, aren't you?
incorrect: You are a teacher, isn't it?

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use look for to mean search
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa look for con el sentido de buscar
grammarRules.explanation: Look for means search for something.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Look for significa buscar algo.
examples: I am looking for my keys

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use since for a starting point and for for a duration
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa since para punto inicial y for para duración
grammarRules.explanation: Use since + starting point and for + duration in common present-perfect contexts.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa since + punto inicial y for + duración.
examples: I have worked here for five years
incorrect: I have worked here since five years

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

grammarRules.title: Use used to for past habits or states
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa used to para hábitos o estados pasados
grammarRules.explanation: Used to + base verb describes past habits or states that are no longer regular.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base describe hábitos o estados pasados que ya no son habituales.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.
